items.implementationGap: Dependencies are installed independently for each hosted worker.
items.governingRequirement: Part II section 4 prepared immutable dependency environment.
items.expectedBenefit: Eliminate repeated dependency materialization and reduce queue-exposed wall time.
items.correctnessInvariant: Restore only an exact OS, Node, lockfile, package-manager, and install-policy identity.
items.dependencyRisk: Artifact provenance, cache poisoning, and platform drift.

items.implementationGap: DB-required workers still migrate and seed their own disposable database.
items.governingRequirement: Part II section 5 build-once, clone-many certified baseline.
items.expectedBenefit: Remove repeated migration and seed setup while retaining run-owned mutable clones.
items.correctnessInvariant: Baseline hash, migrations, fixture policy, and generated-client identity are verified; every run mutates only a clone.
items.dependencyRisk: Baseline corruption or stale fixture identity.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Prepared artifacts and certified SQLite baseline.

items.implementationGap: Each selected suite receives a separate hosted worker.
items.governingRequirement: Part II section 6 compatible multi-suite workers with per-suite receipts.
items.expectedBenefit: Reduce VM startup and dependency setup repetition.
items.correctnessInvariant: Logical-suite receipts, case counts, result, and cleanup stay independent.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Worker bundling and per-suite receipt integrity.

items.implementationGap: Workflow waves remain static even though obvious host-global serialization is removed.
items.governingRequirement: Part II sections 7 and 9 typed capacities and dependency-ready scheduling.
items.expectedBenefit: Shorter critical path without unsafe contention.
items.correctnessInvariant: Only capacity-exhausted declared shared resources serialize execution.

items.implementationGap: Browser adapter retains the compatibility fixed-port path and no dedicated dual-lane broker.
items.governingRequirement: Part II sections 7 and 8 isolated browser lanes and run-owned endpoints.
items.expectedBenefit: Overlap independent browser proof and remove fixed-port contention.
items.correctnessInvariant: Each lane owns port, server identity, DB clone, storage, browser context, and evidence root.
items.dependencyRisk: Cross-lane traffic or stale server identity.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Dynamic port broker and dual browser lanes.

items.implementationGap: No automatic Evidence Invalidation Manifest or derived carry-forward receipt execution exists.
items.governingRequirement: Part I sections 5 and 6 and Part III section 10.
items.expectedBenefit: Avoid re-running semantically unchanged evidence after narrow changes or unrelated main advances.
items.correctnessInvariant: Every mandatory obligation has exactly one current fresh, preserved, or rebound producer; unknown relations rerun fail closed.
items.dependencyRisk: Stale evidence accepted through incomplete dependency analysis.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Evidence Invalidation Manifest and immutable carry-forward receipts.

items.implementationGap: Record-only closure remains a target architecture rather than an executable dedicated gate.
items.governingRequirement: Part I section 8 and Part III section 9.
items.expectedBenefit: Remove browser/build/database tax from non-executable record work.
items.correctnessInvariant: Executable proof is selected only when record changes alter executable semantics.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Record-closure gate with semantic escalation checks.

items.implementationGap: Telemetry exposes setup timing but does not yet open or enforce policy incidents for repeated broad reruns.
items.expectedBenefit: Make verification churn visible and remediable.
items.correctnessInvariant: No incident mechanism may weaken mandatory proof.
items.dependencyRisk: False incident attribution without manifest data.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Invalidation-aware duplicate-run detector and incident records.

items.implementationGap: Worker telemetry is machine-readable but lacks a complete hosted queue and critical-path UI.
items.governingRequirement: Part I section 11 and Part II section 11.
items.expectedBenefit: Distinguish queue, setup, execution, teardown, upload, and finalization bottlenecks.
items.correctnessInvariant: Telemetry is diagnostic and cannot alter RELEASE_GO semantics.
items.dependencyRisk: GitHub timestamp availability and misleading aggregate reporting.
items.recommendedNextSlice: Hosted-run critical-path summary and queue timestamp adapter.
